units.reason: Range satisfaction needs a semver operator. normalize: semver-major is exact only for a caret range from N.0.0: Stage B showed a pass with engines ^12.5.0 and pnpm@12.4.1, which pnpm refuses, and a finding with >=11, which pnpm accepts. The normalize matches only a caret range starting at N.0.0. Section 2.2 names a semver-range operator as B-adapter, the same gap Stage A cited for trpc-06.
The record text still described the bucket or rule from before Stage B or the integrator changed it.

It is an intra-file reference, and today's kinds express it. Caveat: the tools strip HTML comments before checking and the regex does not; the clone has no commented-out includes.

removed.summary: manypkg ROOT_HAS_PROD_DEPENDENCIES: the private root package.json declares no `dependencies`, only devDependencies
removed.why: Not shown to be enforced. Stage A inferred a ROOT_HAS_PROD_DEPENDENCIES check only from the clone passing the merge-queue diff. As far as I recall, manypkg's documented root check is the opposite, ROOT_HAS_DEV_DEPENDENCIES (root dependencies belong in `dependencies`; I could not verify this offline). trpc's root has 35 devDependencies and 0 dependencies, so that check would fail it. cloudflare/workers-sdk on manypkg 0.23.0 keeps its root in dependencies (19 dependencies, 0 devDependencies). The evidence fits 'manypkg 0.25.1 checks no root field' at least as well as Stage A's reading. Move it to value-add or drop it.

value_add: alint://bundled/toolchain-pins@v1: .nvmrc holds an exact version; .tool-versions `nodejs` equals .nvmrc. Both are kept by hand: renovate's nvm manager, node-version datasource and pnpm updates are disabled, and nothing checks them.
alint://bundled/hygiene/lockfiles@v1: only the root pnpm-lock.yaml. trpc only gitignores package-lock.json/yarn.lock.
alint://bundled/monorepo/pnpm-workspace@v1: pnpm-workspace.yaml declares packages; packages/* have a README and a name.
trpc-va-lockstep-versions: every packages/* version equals packages/server's. tooling/release writes this; nothing checks it between releases.
trpc-va-internal-peers-pinned: peerDependencies on @trpc/server/client/react-query equal the released version.
trpc-va-engines-node-major-matches-nvmrc: root and www engines.node share .nvmrc's major. pnpm only warns on an engines.node mismatch because no engine-strict is set, so it is not enforced.
trpc-va-server-license-matches-root: packages/server/LICENSE is identical to the root LICENSE.
trpc-root-no-prod-dependencies (info): kept as value-add after trpc-09 was removed; see `removed`
absent_categories: locale / i18n: no locale catalogs, translation files or i18n gate; the docs are English-only
pre-commit hooks: no husky, lefthook, pre-commit, lint-staged or simple-git-hooks
non-GitHub CI: no .gitlab-ci, .circleci, azure-pipelines, Jenkinsfile, .buildkite; Vercel builds www externally
Makefile/justfile/Taskfile: none; tasks are package.json scripts and turbo
dedicated dep-version tools: no syncpack, sherif, yarn constraints or knip; manypkg runs with no config block (no workspaceProtocol: require, no ignoredRules)
pnpm catalogMode / engine-strict / .npmrc at the root: none, so catalog use is not mandated and engines.node only warns
toolchain pins: no .node-version, Volta or Dockerfile; Node via .nvmrc (+ an unenforced .tool-versions), pnpm via packageManager
per-file license headers / SPDX: none (root MIT LICENSE plus a copy in packages/server)
changesets / CHANGELOG gate: none; release notes are generated from PRs at release
dependency audit or license compliance gate: none (CodeQL only)
manypkg INCORRECT_REPOSITORY_FIELD: inactive, because the root package.json has no `repository` field
unusual: The lint workflow is named 'autofix.ci' for the autofix-ci app. On PRs, the oxlint/manypkg/oxfmt fixes are committed back rather than failing. Only the merge queue (and release commits on main) fail, through `git diff --exit-code`.

Catalogs plus manypkg: manypkg ignores catalog:/npm:/workspace: specifiers, so EXTERNAL_MISMATCH governs only literal semver ranges. The repo carries a catalog value and a different literal range for the same dependency (catalog next ^16.4.5 vs ^15.5.29 in 13 examples; oxfmt ^0.77.0 vs ^0.75.0; typescript ^7.0.2 / ts-api ^6.0.3 / www 5.9.3 vs a literal ^5.9.2 x34), and nothing checks drift between catalogs and literals.

Examples depend on @trpc/* through bare `npm:@trpc/<name>` aliases (no version) rather than workspace:. There are also `npm:zod@^3.0.0` and `npm:next-auth@^4.24.15` aliases, and one example pins @trpc/* to ^11.16.0.

subtree.yml's standalone conversion (tooling/subtree) works as a dependency-version gate for 10 examples published to trpc/examples-<name>: every catalog: must resolve, and workspace: is allowed only for @shared/ui and @trpc/*. It also inlines @shared/ui sources and checks imports against declared dependencies.

Docs frontmatter (`skill:` blocks in www/v11/docs) drives generated TanStack Intent agent skills, which are not committed (prepack writes them). The generator validates cross-references: unique names, package plus keyword, requires/include/references, and that the skills page lists exactly the shipped skills. Six B-adapter units all hinge on a missing Markdown-frontmatter adapter.

Agent-skill vendoring: .agents/skills holds both installed and written skills. skills-lock.json pins the installed ones with a CLI-specific computedHash, NOTICE-pstack.md records the pinned commit, every skill has a .claude/skills symlink, and .oxfmtrc.json negation entries decide which skills get formatted. All of this is documented in AGENTS.md.

tooling/release writes lockstep versions (@trpc/openapi stays an -alpha prerelease), pins internal peerDependencies to the released version, and checks for public-package dependency cycles on every canary. Only at a stable release does it check that the frozen lockfile still applies and that the build changes nothing. The build regenerates package.json exports/files/funding/peer typescript and per-package turbo.json via scripts/entrypoints.ts.
All e2e jobs (examples, Deno, Bun, legacy Node 20/22) are continue-on-error, so they are advisory and not counted.

Toolchain: CI takes Node from .nvmrc everywhere except subtree.yml (24.x) and the legacy matrix. pnpm comes from packageManager. engines.pnpm is a hard pnpm check but engines.node only a warning. Examples declare their own packageManager pnpm@10.33.1 and engines >=20 / >=18.15.0 for standalone use.
vitest.shared.ts builds its @trpc/* aliases from each packages/*/package.json `exports`. That is an implicit requirement that every non-test package declares exports; it is not counted as a unit.
www/sponsors.json and the README sponsors blocks are bot-maintained by a scheduled workflow, and tests guard the markers and the data's uniqueness.
The .coderabbit.yaml path instructions flag generated directories for AI review. They are guidance, not a gate.
check_result: `alint validate-config` passed: 63 rules loaded (3 bundles plus 36 repo rules). `alint -c CONFIG check . --compact` on the clone reported 'all rules passed', with zero violations, so no rule needs an explanation. Every A and C rule was also shown to fire on a broken scratch copy, and so was every value-add rule. The scratch tree was removed afterwards, and the clone's `git status --porcelain` is empty.
stage_b_config_issues: Reproduced: validate-config reports 63 rules and check passes on the clone with zero violations. The clone's git status is clean afterwards.

trpc-nvmrc-version-spec (trpc-01) is stricter than setup-node. It fires on '^24', which setup-node resolves (it accepts semver ranges from node-version-file). Stage A's '>=24 <25' fire test therefore shows a false positive, not the invariant. Relax it to a non-empty single-token spec, or accept ranges. Deletion, an empty file and 'twenty-four' fire correctly.

trpc-package-manager-pnpm-pinned (trpc-02) covers only the branch where no version is given. pnpm/action-setup also fails ('Multiple versions of pnpm specified') when a step's with.version disagrees with packageManager. Two yaml_path_absent rules, on $.jobs.*.steps[?match(@.uses, '^pnpm/action-setup@.+')].with.version over .github/workflows/*.yml and on $.runs.steps[...] over .github/setup/action.yml, pass on the clone and fired on scratch copies with `version: 11.0.0` added. A cross_file equals against packageManager would be exact. The removal, yarn@ and +sha512 hash cases behave correctly.
trpc-package-manager-satisfies-engines-pnpm (trpc-03) gets both directions wrong (reproduced): engines.pnpm ^12.5.0 passes and >=11 fires. See reclassify.
trpc-root-no-prod-dependencies (trpc-09) is presented as an enforced manypkg check, but no such check is established. See remove. Demote it to value-add at level info, or drop it.

trpc-subtree-examples-workspace-protocol (trpc-11) is line-based. A workspace: entry on the same line as `"dependencies": {` is not selected (reproduced on a scratch copy). oxfmt keeps a one-line object that fits in 80 columns, so 'oxfmt keeps one dependency per line' is not guaranteed. The risk is low; the single-line and nested-manifest cases fire as Stage A said.
trpc-agent-skill-has-claude-link (trpc-16) uses dir_exists, which follows the symlink, so a copied directory passes. See reclassify.

trpc-published-readmes-have-sponsor-markers (trpc-22) also covers the root README.md. The CI test (www/build/sponsors-sync.test.ts:713-731) checks only packages/*. Only the scheduled, secret-gated sponsors.yml sync (sponsors-sync.ts:203) fails on the root README, and it runs after merge.

trpc-workspace-package-names-valid (trpc-14) does not cover validate-npm-package-name's core-module and blacklisted names: 'http' and 'node_modules' pass the regex. Coverage itself is right: the globs select exactly the 59 workspace manifests, hidden examples/.test and .experimental members included (checked with a counting rule).

Record facts: trpc-07 says there are 33 peer entries; the clone has 32 (packages/* 30, tooling/ui 2). trpc-26's evidence omits that CI also decodes every v11 docs page's frontmatter in www/build/content.ts:112-147 (title, section and a numeric order are required; experiment is an enum) through the www tests. It is the same unit with wider evidence.

Value-add labelling is otherwise accurate. The three bundles and the five trpc-va-* rules are commented VALUE-ADD, and the trpc-va-* rules use level info. The bundles keep their own levels. monorepo/pnpm-workspace's 'members have a name' overlaps an enforced check: tooling/release/src/workspace.ts:28-30 throws '<file> has no name' on every canary.
stage_b_summary:
Stage A's record is careful, but it has one unverified A unit, three classifications that do not hold up, and five missed units.

**Removed:** trpc-09. Stage A inferred a manypkg ROOT_HAS_PROD_DEPENDENCIES check from the clone passing. As I recall it, manypkg's documented root check runs the other way (ROOT_HAS_DEV_DEPENDENCIES), which trpc's devDependencies-only root would fail; I could not confirm this offline. The evidence fits 'no root check in 0.25.1' at least as well.

**Reclassified:**
- trpc-03, C to B-adapter: the semver-major approximation is wrong in both directions (reproduced).
- trpc-16, A to B-adapter: dir_exists cannot tell the required symlink from a copied directory (R4).
- trpc-57, D to B-delegate: by R7, the Docusaurus admonition checks run over Markdown files alint reads. CI applies them to every v11 docs page through the www tests, not only to skill pages.

**Missed:**
- trpc-B01, dep-version, A: workspace: specifiers must name workspace projects. Under the ruling Stage A used for trpc-10, this is a lookup; a cross_file superset expresses it today, and it was fire-verified both ways.
- trpc-B02, other, A: Twoslash `// @include:` lines must resolve to include blocks in the same file. This is split from the compile check (D); for_each_file plus cross_file subset expresses it, and it was fire-verified.
- trpc-B03, B-adapter: the subtree @source brace lists must name existing files. registry_paths_resolve with entries_are_globs accepts a nonexistent alternative and a wildcard.
- trpc-B04, C: the reserved src/shared-ui directory guard in the subtree conversion.
- trpc-B05, B-config unique-key: workspace names must be unique for turbo. This rests on tool knowledge and was not verified offline.

**Fire tests reproduced on my own scratch copy:**
- trpc-01 fires as claimed, but also on '^24', which setup-node accepts.
- trpc-02 fires as claimed. It does not cover action-setup's conflicting-version error; a yaml_path_absent rule that does was verified.
- trpc-11 fires as claimed, with a narrow false negative on a one-line dependencies object.
- trpc-12 (C) fires as claimed.

I also confirmed that ordered_block cannot express UNSORTED_DEPENDENCIES: exact end markers either leave a block unclosed or run past it. trpc-15 therefore stays B-adapter.

**Revised counts:** A=10 (01, 02, 11, 14, 18, 20, 21, 23, B01, B02), C=5 (12, 19, 22, 30, B04), B=21 (B-config 7: 05, 07, 08, 10, 17, 24, B05; B-adapter 13: 03, 06, 13, 15, 16, 25-29, 31, 32, B03; B-delegate 1: 57), D=29.
- coverage_today = 10/36 = 28%
- coverage_with_tuning = 15/36 = 42%
- gap = 21/36 = 58%

**Per family:**

| Family | A | C | B | Today | With tuning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| toolchain-pin | 2 | 0 | 1 | 2/3 | 2/3 |
| dep-version | 2 | 1 | 5 | 2/8 | 3/8 |
| other | 6 | 4 | 15 | 6/25 | 10/25 |

There are no locale units. After the slice, 05, 24 and B05 (unique-key) would make 13/36 = 36%.

**Unverified leads, not counted:**
- manypkg INTERNAL_DEV_DEP_NOT_STAR. The clone is consistent with it: all internal devDependencies are workspace:* or npm: aliases.
- packageManager equal to pnpm-lock.yaml's packageManagerDependencies.pnpm (12.4.1 in both). This is likely D under R7 as lockfile freshness.
- The www build (docs broken links, parent/section) runs only on Vercel. If that check is not a required gate, trpc-64 is not enforced either. If it is a gate, its docs-content checks are missing units.
- trpc-12 versus trpc-61 is a possible double count (a precondition and its only detector); I left both as Stage A had them.

Scratch dir <scratch>/trpc-trpc-b/ has been removed. Nothing from the repository ran, and no network was used.
notes:
Counts (D excluded from ratios): A=10 (01,02,09,11,14,16,18,20,21,23), C=5 (03,12,19,22,30), B=16 (B-config 6: 05,07,08,10,17,24; B-adapter 10: 06,13,15,25,26,27,28,29,31,32), D=30 (40-69). coverage_today = 10/31 = 32%; coverage_with_tuning = 15/31 = 48%; gap = 16/31 = 52%. Per family: toolchain-pin A2 C1 B0 (2/3 today, 3/3 with tuning); dep-version A2 C1 B-config4 B-adapter1, plus D2 (56, 61), giving 2/8 today and 3/8 with tuning; other A6 C3 B-config2 B-adapter9 (6/20); locale: none. After the slice (equality/unique-key/cardinality), trpc-05 and trpc-24 (unique-key) would move to A if phase 8 confirms, giving 12/31 = 39%. The remaining B-config units are set (07, 08, 17) and reference (10).

Uncertainties, stated honestly:
(1) The manypkg check list (EXTERNAL_MISMATCH, INTERNAL_MISMATCH, INVALID_DEV_AND_PEER_DEPENDENCY_RELATIONSHIP, MULTIPLE_DEPENDENCY_TYPES, INVALID_PACKAGE_NAME, UNSORTED_DEPENDENCIES, the root-dependencies check, INCORRECT_REPOSITORY_FIELD) comes from manypkg's documented checks. The @manypkg/cli 0.25.1 source was not available offline; its dependency list in pnpm-lock.yaml (validate-npm-package-name, sembear, semver, parse-github-url) is consistent with it. That the root check is ROOT_HAS_PROD_DEPENDENCIES (root deps belong in devDependencies) is inferred: trpc's devDependencies-only root passes the merge-queue diff gate. I could not confirm whether INVALID_DEV_AND_PEER also compares ranges. The clone state matches every check: one literal semver range per external dependency, all maps sorted, no duplicate dependency types, every peer also a devDependency.
(2) pnpm engine behavior is from my knowledge of pnpm's packageIsInstallable: an engines.pnpm mismatch throws, while an engines.node mismatch only warns without engine-strict. On that basis Node-vs-engines.node is not a unit (it is value-add), and trpc-03 is.
(3) I took pnpm 12's defaults for frozen-lockfile-in-CI and strictDepBuilds from memory, and folded them into the D unit trpc-56.
(4) Classifying unicorn/filename-case (trpc-30) by its logic rather than as a linter D unit is a judgement under R7. Stage B may move it to D under R2.
(5) trpc-12 counts a load-bearing code-comment convention (R5) as distinct from the release's frozen-lockfile D check (trpc-61).
(6) trpc-16 does not distinguish a symlink from a copied directory.
(7) SK units 26-29 and 31-32 are counted one per distinct generator assertion (R1: one script's one assertion).
File-graph edge sources: 2, neither expressible today: package-name dependency edges for the cycle check (trpc-13), and docs URL-to-page/anchor references from TS sources (trpc-25). The workspace globs in trpc-14 mirror pnpm-workspace.yaml (59 manifests); the nested examples/.experimental/next-app-dir/src/trpc/package.json is not a workspace member and is correctly excluded. No network was used, nothing from the repo ran, and the scratch dir <scratch>/trpc-trpc-a/ has been removed.

changes.detail: Replaced the strict regex with a verbose (?x) block-scalar regex. It accepts an exact or partial version (24, 24.1.0, v24.1.0, 24.x), semver ranges (^24, ~24.1, >=24 <25, 24 - 25, >=22 || ^24), an optional node/nodejs prefix, and the aliases lts/*, lts/<codename>, lts/-N, node, latest and current. Surrounding blank lines are allowed. Passes on the clone (24.22.2). On a scratch copy of .nvmrc it passed on ^24, >=24 <25, 24, 24.1.0 and lts/*. It fired on an empty file and on 'twenty-four' (an earlier prototype run also fired on whitespace-only, '24 abc' and '24.22.2.1'). Deleting .nvmrc fired trpc-nvmrc-present, and the spec rule stayed silent because there is no file to read. A comment records the approximation: setup-node takes the first single-token line of a multi-line file, while this rule wants exactly one spec.

yaml_path_absent on .github/workflows/*.yml, path $.jobs.*.steps[?match(@.uses, '^pnpm/action-setup@.+')].with.version (Stage B's form). Passes on the clone. On a scratch copy it fired with `with: version: 11.0.0` added to the subtree.yml action-setup step, and with `version: 12.4.1` added to the sponsors.yml step. It was silent after restoring both. The comment says it is stricter than action-setup for a version equal to packageManager's (Stage B: action-setup fails only on disagreement; a cross_file equals would be exact).

yaml_path_absent on .github/setup/action.yml, path $.runs.steps[?match(@.uses, '^pnpm/action-setup@.+')].with.version. Passes on the clone. It fired on a scratch copy with `with: version: 11.0.0` added to the composite action's action-setup step, and was silent after the restore.

Moved to the VALUE-ADD section at level info, with a comment that unit trpc-09 was removed because no manypkg root check is established. The message is now prefixed VALUE-ADD and the id is unchanged. Passes on the clone. Adding a root `dependencies` block on a scratch copy produced an info finding.

Moved to the VALUE-ADD section at level info and labelled as a major-band approximation. The comment names the limitation: normalize: semver-major is not range satisfaction and is wrong both ways (^12.5.0 with pnpm@12.4.1 passes; >=11 fires), so the unit needs a semver-range operator. Passes on the clone. engines.pnpm ^11.0.0 on a scratch copy produced an info finding.

Moved to the VALUE-ADD section at level info and labelled as an approximation. The comment says dir_exists follows the link, so a copied directory passes and only a missing link fires; alint has no symlink predicate, and no_symlinks is the inverse. Only the level and message changed. Passes on the clone. Not re-fire-tested.

cross_file relation superset. The source unions $.name from a single brace glob that mirrors pnpm-workspace.yaml's 12 member globs (root included). A counting rule confirmed the glob selects exactly the 59 workspace manifests, the same set as a find over the member globs. The targets use the same glob with regex '"([^"]+)"\s*:\s*"workspace:', and allow_missing_target is true. Passes on the clone. On a scratch copy of the 59 manifests it fired on examples/.test/monotest-app with @monotest/api renamed to @monotest/apix workspace:*. Renaming tooling/ui to @shared/uikit fired on all 6 @shared/ui dependents (the 5 examples plus www). Adding "@trpc/nonexistent": "workspace:^" to www/package.json fired. It was silent after the restore.

for_each_file over www/v11/docs/**/*.md, www/v11/home/**/*.md and www/blog/**/*.md, with a nested cross_file relation subset. The source regex '(?m)^[ \t>]*// @include: (\S+)[ \t]*$' and the target regex '(?m)^[ \t>]*`{3,}twoslash include (\S+)' both read {path}. Passes on the clone (133 // @include: lines under www/v11). On a scratch copy of the 102 .md files it fired in four cases: renaming one quickstart.md reference to trpcx, renaming the `server` include block to serverx, appending an @include to www/blog/README.md (a file with no include blocks), and appending a blockquoted @include to www/v11/home/step-3.md. It was silent after the restore. The comment says the regexes see the whole file, while the tools strip HTML comments and expand only inside Twoslash fences, and ~~~ fences are not matched.

dir_absent over the 5 hand-listed @shared/ui dependents' src/shared-ui. Those are examples/.experimental/next-app-dir, next-minimal-starter, next-prisma-starter, next-prisma-websockets-starter and tanstack-start-sse-chat; grep confirms they are the only example manifests depending on @shared/ui, and all have src/. Passes on the clone. On a scratch tree it fired on examples/next-minimal-starter/src/shared-ui/button.tsx and on an empty examples/.experimental/next-app-dir/src/shared-ui. It stayed silent on a non-dependent examples/minimal/src/shared-ui. The C reason is in the comment: dependents are listed by hand.
Added a gap note: validate-npm-package-name also rejects Node core-module names and its blacklist, and those pass the regex (`http`, `node_modules`), so they are not covered. The rule is unchanged.

Updated the header summary. It drops 'root-deps', adds workspace: resolution, the shared-ui guard and Twoslash include resolution, and says trpc-03/trpc-16 (B-adapter) and trpc-09 (removed) are kept only as VALUE-ADD approximations at level info.
